theme: 3 terms on self inside escaping closures: writing self in front of a property, capturing self weakly, and the cases where you may leave self out

terms.definition: Writing `self.` in front of a property inside an escaping closure, which a class requires so you can see the capture.
terms.example: The compiler wants Explicit Self here, because this closure outlives the method.

terms.definition: Writing `[weak self]` in a closure's capture list, so the closure does not keep its object alive.
terms.example: Use Weak Self in that network callback, or the view model never gets freed.

terms.definition: Leaving out `self.` inside a closure, allowed after `[self]` in the capture list or after `guard let self`.
terms.example: After `guard let self`, Implicit Self is fine, so drop all those `self.` prefixes.

video.description:
Learn to explain self in escaping closures in Swift: Explicit Self, Weak Self & Implicit Self, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Explicit Self - Writing `self.` in front of a property inside an escaping closure, which a class requires so you can see the capture.
Weak Self - Writing `[weak self]` in a closure's capture list, so the closure does not keep its object alive.
Implicit Self - Leaving out `self.` inside a closure, allowed after `[self]` in the capture list or after `guard let self`.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Explicit Self, Weak Self & Implicit Self in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
명시적 self, 약한 self, 암시적 self 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Explicit Self - Writing `self.` in front of a property inside an escaping closure, which a class requires so you can see the capture.
한국어: 명시적 self: 이스케이핑 클로저 안에서 프로퍼티 앞에 `self.`를 쓰는 것으로, 클래스는 캡처가 보이도록 이것을 요구함

Weak Self - Writing `[weak self]` in a closure's capture list, so the closure does not keep its object alive.
한국어: 약한 self: 클로저 캡처 목록에 `[weak self]`를 써서 클로저가 객체를 살려 두지 않게 하는 것

Implicit Self - Leaving out `self.` inside a closure, allowed after `[self]` in the capture list or after `guard let self`.
한국어: 암시적 self: 캡처 목록에 `[self]`를 쓰거나 `guard let self` 이후에 클로저 안에서 `self.`를 생략하는 것

landscape.hook: No self in the closure, and it still compiles. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Where did self go?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `start` uses `title` without `self`. Is that allowed in an escaping closure?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Usually not. A class needs Explicit Self there, so you see the capture.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So why does this one compile?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because of `guard let self`. After it, Implicit Self is allowed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And what does Weak Self do first?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Weak Self captures the player weakly, so the closure doesn't keep it alive.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So if the screen closes, `self` becomes `nil`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, and the `guard` just returns. Nothing is printed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Should I still write Explicit Self, for clarity?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Your call. Some teams prefer it, but with Weak Self and guard, Implicit Self reads fine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: OK, I'll keep it short then.
Escaping closure in a class? Swift wants Explicit Self.
